implementation_notes: Ruby's messaging stacks expose the enricher as middleware: Sidekiq client middleware mutates the job payload before it is pushed (job["customer"] = Customer.current_id) and server middleware runs around processing, so enrichment is added to the chain in an initializer instead of being a component; Hash#merge (with a conflict block) is the merge primitive and makes field precedence explicit. Rack middleware plays the same role for HTTP layers. The resource access itself stays a hand-written repository object behind the middleware.
code_sketch:
class EnrichOrderMiddleware
  include Sidekiq::ClientMiddleware            # Sidekiq 7+ requires the mixin

  def call(job_class, job, queue, redis_pool)
    customer = CustomerRepo.find(job["customer_id"])
    job["customer_name"] = customer&.name      # merge into the payload
    job["region"] = customer&.region
    yield
  end
end
# Sidekiq.configure_client { |c| c.client_middleware { |chain| chain.add EnrichOrderMiddleware } }
pitfalls: The job hash is the payload persisted in Redis: enrichment done in client middleware is frozen into the job, so later reference-data changes never reach it (good for audit, bad for freshness).

Client middleware registered only in configure_client does not run for jobs that the server process itself pushes (workers enqueue follow-up jobs), so Sidekiq requires registering it in configure_server as well.
An exception in middleware stops the job from being pushed at all; catch resource errors when enrichment is optional.
